EXTRA CLASS · QUESTION WORDS · 16 CARDS · AGES 3–5

Question words flashcards — the sixteen questions little kids ask first.

Sixteen printable question word cards for ages three to five: who, what, when, where, why and how lead the deck, and ten more questions — how many, whose turn, what happens next — follow behind. Every card below prints free, downloads as a full-size image and carries one plain tip on how to ask it together tonight. The whole class lives on this single page.

More extra classes ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Print the card. Ask the question. All week long.

Pick one question card a week and pin it to the fridge at your child’s eye level. Ask it yourself a few times a day — at snack time, in the bath, on the walk — then hand the question over: children who get to do the asking learn the word twice as fast. A question card on the fridge gets noticed every single day, and noticed is how words stick.

The six core questions come first because they open every conversation your child will ever have: who, what, when, where, why and how. The ten that follow grow out of real life — counting crackers, taking turns, hiding under a blanket — so print them in any order your days need. Everything on this page is free to print at home, today.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the questions are asked next.

Where is your nose? in Class 21 · Ages 3–4 ↗Questions about the story in Class 29 · Ages 4–5 ↗Why and how in Class 30 · Ages 4–5 ↗The parents’ shelf in the library · All 16 cards ↗All the extra classes ↗

Class 21 answers questions about your child’s own body, Class 29 asks who and what-next about every story, and Class 30 thinks through why and how — the question cards hand your child the words to join in. This page is the lesson: it teaches each question the way a teacher would. Parents who want the whole deck on one wall will find it on the parents’ shelf in the flashcards library: the same sixteen cards, downloading and printing straight from there.

A question is an invitation. Every card on this page hands your child the words to start one — and a child who asks is a child who is already learning.
